props.title: Three Addresses

B01.capture_spec: C01: scene script capture-scenes/capture-c01.gd (CAPTURE-PLAN.md): faint backdrop ColorRect (02-sky-world, alpha 0.35), blob sprites (256 px art, scale 1) at y=240, left with 01-sky-local.gdshader from x=220, right with 02-sky-world.gdshader from x=700; both slide +300 over 10 to 56 % of the beat (ease in-out) and rest; 14 s, 30 fps, Forward+, no input (CAPTURE-PLAN.md).
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Three Addresses' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window: a faint copy of a star sky (indigo, cream stars, a ringed planet) behind two test sprites in one row. Both slide right together, slowly. Stars inside the left sprite travel with it; the right sprite uncovers the planet and stars that stay where they are, lining up with the faint copy. Labels: 'from the sprite' under the left, 'from the world' under the right.
B01.motion_claim: Both sprites make the same slide, but only the left one's stars move with it; the right one uncovers a planet that does not move.

show.event: two sprites on a faint sky, labelled
both slide right while the voice describes the left, then the right
the right sprite is over the planet; its picture matches the faint copy, the left one's does not

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of two sprites with dots inside
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of 'carries its stars' against 'slides over fixed stars'; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: A plane of outline cells (pixel grid, no fill). A terracotta dot sits fixed at one cell. A zero marker (a ring with a right arrow and a down arrow) sits at the top-left with a live readout '5 across · 4 down'. The zero marker then slides to a cell four across and one down; the readout counts to '1 across · 3 down' while the dot never moves.
B02.motion_claim: The zero slides across the grid and the two numbers change continuously while the dot stays where it is.

show.event: grid, dot, zero marker, '5 across · 4 down'
the zero starts to slide
'1 across · 3 down', dot unmoved

B02.why: The claim is that the numbers change and the dot does not; a moving zero with a live readout shows both at once, a table only lists them.

B03.visual_intent: One scene on the cream stage: a large outlined rectangle for the world with a zero marker at its top-left labelled 'world space'; inside it a smaller outlined rectangle for the window; inside that a sprite (square outline with the test blob) with a zero marker at its center labelled 'local space'; a third zero marker at the window's top-left labelled 'screen space'. Short definitions appear with each label: 'from the node's own zero', 'from the world's origin' and, for the third, the glossary wording 'pixels of the window, counted from the top left, y growing downward'. A terracotta dot marks the sprite's top-left corner and stays through the act.
B03.motion_claim: The three zero markers land one by one, each with its label, in the same picture.

show.event: world, window and sprite outlines
local zero at the sprite's center
world zero lands before the midpoint
screen zero at the window's corner
the corner dot, one corner with an address in each

B03.why: Three origins have to be seen in one picture to be compared; a diagram with the world, the window and the sprite nested is the claim.

B04.visual_intent: The same diagram zoomed on the sprite: its center zero marker with a right arrow and a down arrow, a '128' dimension across the top, and a grey arrow from the zero to the terracotta corner dot with the tag '(-64, -64)'. The sprite, its zero and its arrow then slide to the right across the world; the tag does not change.
B04.motion_claim: The sprite slides away with its zero and its arrow; the tag '(-64, -64)' stays exactly the same.

show.event: sprite, local zero, arrow to the corner, tag
dimension '128' lands
sprite slides right, tag unchanged

B04.runner_up: ShaderLab capture of a color-coded sprite
B04.why: Local numbers are about one sprite and its own zero; a sprite sliding off with its tag unchanged shows 'that answer holds' as motion.

B05.visual_intent: The world rectangle with its zero marker at the top-left. A long grey arrow runs from the world zero to the terracotta corner dot with the tag '(536, 336)'; a small grey tag '(-64, -64)' stays beside the sprite. The sprite slides right by a hundred: the arrow stretches and the world tag counts up to '(636, 336)' while the small local tag does not move.
B05.motion_claim: The long arrow from the world's origin stretches as the sprite slides; its tag counts up while the local tag stays put.

show.event: arrow from the world zero, tag (536, 336)
sprite starts to slide
tag (636, 336); local tag unchanged

B05.why: The world address is a distance from far away; an arrow that stretches while a number counts is that distance as motion.

B06.visual_intent: The world rectangle, with the window rectangle (the camera's view) drawn on it and its own top-left zero marker labelled 'screen space'. A grey arrow runs from the window's zero to the terracotta corner dot with the tag '(286, 236)'. A small camera mark sits at the window's center; the world zero and its '(536, 336)' tag stay faintly visible.
B06.motion_claim: The arrow from the window's corner draws out to the dot and its tag lands; the world tag stays where it was.

show.event: window frame with its own zero and a camera mark
arrow from the window's corner to the dot

B06.runner_up: ShaderLab capture of the same scene
B06.why: The window and the camera are diagram objects; showing the window as a frame laid over the world is the only way to see 'zero is the window's corner'.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · 1280 by 720 window · camera pans right by 100 · scripted run

B07.capture_spec: C02: scene script capture-scenes/capture-c02.gd: Camera2D (890,460) to (990,460) over 12 to 40 % of the beat (ease in-out), sprite (600,400) 128 px art scale 1 with a drawn cream box and a terracotta corner dot (radius 6), backdrop sky ColorRect (alpha 0.5) covering world (0,0) to (2000,1000); 13 s (CAPTURE-PLAN.md).
B07.visual_intent: A real Godot render: a faint star sky as the world, a 128 px test sprite in a thin cream box with a terracotta dot on its top-left corner, and a camera that pans right by a hundred. Readouts: 'world 536, 336' stays; 'screen 286, 236' changes to 'screen 186, 236' as the sprite and the whole sky slide left.
B07.motion_claim: The corner dot slides left on screen while its world readout never changes.

show.event: sprite, corner dot, readouts world 536, 336 and screen 286, 236
camera pans right by 100; everything slides left
readout becomes screen 186, 236; world readout unchanged

B07.runner_up: manim: a window sliding over the world with ticking numbers
B07.why: A real camera pan in a real render is the evidence; the numbers are measured, and the sky makes the sliding visible.
